confidence: Recomputed from recovered historical matchups and verified winners-bracket participants.

categories.title: The Impossible Comeback
categories.label: Worst opening start by an eventual champion
categories.detail: Stilly opened 2023 with four straight losses, sat at 1–5 after Week 6, and still won the title as the fourth seed.
categories.rule: Most consecutive losses at the beginning of a champion's regular season.

categories.title: From Rock Bottom to a Ring
categories.label: Deepest losing-record deficit survived by a champion
categories.detail: Stilly reached 0–4 in Week 4 and 1–5 in Week 6 before rallying to 8–6 and winning the 2023 championship.
categories.rule: Largest deficit of losses minus wins at any point in a champion's regular season.

categories.title: The Cinderella Champion
categories.label: Lowest playoff seed to win the championship
categories.detail: Koble entered the 2020 postseason as the sixth seed after a 7–7 regular season and captured the title.
categories.rule: Largest official winners-bracket seed number among champions.
categories.source: Verified ESPN and Sleeper playoff brackets

categories.title: The .500 Champion
categories.label: Most regular-season losses by an eventual champion
categories.detail: Koble went 7–7 in 2020 and still won it all. This is a raw loss count, not adjusted for schedule length.
categories.rule: Largest total regular-season losses among completed championship seasons.

categories.title: The Losing Streak Survivors
categories.label: Longest regular-season losing streak by a champion
categories.detail: Koble lost Weeks 8–11 in 2020; Stilly lost Weeks 1–4 in 2023. Both finished their seasons with a championship.
categories.rule: Longest run of consecutive regular-season losses within a title-winning season; ties retained.

categories.title: The Finals Were Never Guaranteed
categories.label: Worst opening start by a championship finalist
categories.detail: Evans reached the 2021 final after beginning 0–4. Stilly also started 0–4 before winning the 2023 final.
categories.rule: Most opening losses among teams that reached the championship game.

categories.title: The Sixth Seed That Reached the Final
categories.label: Lowest win percentage by a championship finalist
categories.detail: Mitch finished 2023 at 6–8, entered as the sixth seed, and reached the championship game against Stilly.
categories.rule: Lowest regular-season win percentage among championship finalists; ties count as half a win.

categories.title: The Playoff Survivor
categories.label: Lowest win percentage by a playoff qualifier
categories.detail: Thommy made the six-team 2021 championship playoff bracket despite a 5–9 regular season.
categories.rule: Lowest regular-season win percentage among verified championship-bracket participants, excluding consolation teams.

categories.title: The Perfect Six-Week Opening
categories.label: Champions who started 6–0
categories.detail: Birch in 2019 and Thommy in 2024 both won their first six regular-season games and went on to win their championships.
categories.rule: Champions with six recorded wins and no losses through Week 6.

categories.title: The Cruelest Defeat
categories.label: Highest regular-season score in a losing effort
categories.detail: Stew scored 164.80 in Week 10 of 2025 and still lost to Mitch, 167.82–164.80. An extraordinary week with nothing to show in the win column.
categories.rule: Highest recovered regular-season team total in a head-to-head loss; historical ESPN and Sleeper scoring formats differ.

categories.title: The Almost-Perfect Season
categories.label: Best regular-season winning percentage without a championship
categories.detail: Mitch dominated the 2025 regular season at 13–1, entered the playoffs as the No. 1 seed, and watched Scott win the championship.
categories.rule: Highest completed regular-season winning percentage among teams that did not win that season's title; ties count as half-wins.

categories.title: The Season That Refused to Die
categories.label: Deepest regular-season deficit by a playoff qualifier
categories.detail: Thommy in 2021 and Stew in 2025 each sank to 1–6 after Week 7, five games under .500, yet still qualified for the championship playoffs.
categories.rule: Largest losses-minus-wins deficit at any point in a completed regular season, among verified winners-bracket qualifiers; ties retained.
categories.source: 2016–2025 canonical weekly matchups + verified playoff brackets

categories.title: The Greatest Championship Upset
categories.label: Largest positive seed gap overcome to win the final
categories.detail: In 2020, sixth-seeded Koble beat top-seeded Mitch in the championship final—the greatest official seed gap overcome in a title game.
categories.rule: Winner's playoff seed number minus runner-up's playoff seed number for completed championship finals; the largest positive difference wins.
categories.source: Verified ESPN and Sleeper championship finalists, champions and official seeds

categories.title: The Longshot Finalists
categories.label: Lowest-seeded championship runner-ups
categories.detail: Birch reached the 2018 final as the sixth seed before losing to Thommy. Mitch matched that feat in 2023, finishing runner-up to Stilly.
categories.rule: Largest official winners-bracket seed number among teams who reached, but lost, the championship final; ties retained.
categories.source: Verified ESPN and Sleeper championship finalists and bracket seeds

categories.title: The One-Play Exit
categories.label: Closest verified first-round championship-bracket elimination
categories.detail: Tony lost the 2025 opening-round matchup to sixth-seeded Birch, 120.52–119.80. Seven-tenths of a point ended the third seed’s title pursuit.
categories.rule: Smallest absolute score margin in a verified championship-bracket opening round; ignore consolation matchups and missing first-round receipts.
categories.source: Canonical postseason matchup receipts + ESPN/Sleeper official winner-bracket seed maps

categories.title: The Two-Point Door Slam
categories.label: Closest verified championship-bracket semifinal elimination
categories.detail: In the 2024 semifinals, JMid scored 121.08 but fell to eventual champion Thommy’s 123.38. A 2.30-point gap ended the debut-season championship chase.
categories.rule: Smallest absolute score margin in a verified championship-bracket semifinal (2016–2017 two-week aggregate format identified).
categories.source: Verified semifinalists + canonical championship-bracket matchup scores

categories.title: The Four-Point Crown
categories.label: Closest recorded championship final
categories.detail: Tony defeated Evans in the 2021 championship 138.28–133.98, the smallest title-game margin among all ten completed Fellas seasons.
categories.rule: Smallest champion-over-runner-up scoring margin in the official final for seasons 2016–2025; 2016–2017 are two-week aggregates.
categories.source: Verified ESPN/Sleeper final opponents + championship scoring ledger

categories.title: The Ninety-Point Coronation
categories.label: Largest recorded championship-final victory margin
categories.detail: Thommy’s 205.30–114.88 championship victory over Stilly in 2024 delivered a remarkable 90.42-point margin after surviving the semifinal by just 2.30.
categories.rule: Greatest final winning margin from completed championship results; compare as a raw scoreboard record, not as era-adjusted scoring efficiency.
categories.source: Verified championship winner brackets + canonical postseason matchup scores

categories.title: The Almost Champions
categories.label: Most championship-game runner-up finishes without a title
categories.detail: Stew finished runner-up in 2019 and 2022; Mitch finished runner-up in 2020 and 2023. Neither manager had won a championship through the completed 2025 season.
categories.rule: Most verified runner-up finishes among current managers who have zero championships as of the 2025 final. Display each holder’s latest title-game loss; counts include all earlier finals.
categories.source: 2016–2025 official championship final placements + manager identity map

disclosures: 2016 used an eight-team league and four-team playoffs; subsequent fields differ.
ESPN and Sleeper scoring formats changed; these records focus on wins, seeds and finishes rather than point totals.
The archive credits Evans with 2023; JMid entered in 2024.
